series.name: Building Permits
series.source: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
series.source_caveat: FRED mirrors a source with its own lag. For anything time-critical, check the originating agency.

movers.name: Mortgage / 10Y Treasury Spread
movers.notes: MORT30Y minus UST10Y. The single most important spread on the screen.

movers.name: Brent Crude (global benchmark)
movers.notes: Brent Europe spot FOB. The global benchmark: prices roughly two thirds of the world’s traded crude, and it is waterborne, so it carries geopolitical and freight risk that WTI does not.

movers.name: WTI Crude (US benchmark)
movers.notes: West Texas Intermediate, Cushing OK spot FOB. The US benchmark: light, sweet, landlocked. Prices domestic refinery input and therefore US gasoline.

drivers.name: Mortgage spread (w/w)
drivers.detail: Published spread moved +12 bp between PMMS prints

drivers.name: 10Y Treasury
drivers.detail: 10Y -9 bp, passed through at a 0.95 beta

drivers.name: Fed expectations (2Y)
drivers.detail: 2Y -5 bp. The front end is the cleanest free read on Fed repricing while futures probabilities are unavailable.

drivers.name: Average Hourly Earnings
drivers.detail: Average Hourly Earnings 3.02 vs trailing 24m mean (-2.5 sigma). Very bullish for rates

drivers.name: Consumer Price Index
drivers.detail: Consumer Price Index 3.72 vs trailing 24m mean (1.8 sigma). Very bearish for rates

drivers.name: Retail Sales
drivers.detail: Retail Sales 745021 vs trailing 24m mean (2.4 sigma). Very bearish for rates

bullets.text: 10-year Treasury at 5.10%, -9 bp on the day. This is the single biggest input to your rate.
Published 30-year survey at 7.40%, flat week over week. It is a weekly average and always lags your rate sheet.
Mortgage spread 230 bp, normal at the 64th percentile of 10 years. That is 2.30 points of the 7.40% rate coming from spread, not from Treasuries.
10-Year Treasury -9 bp, bigger than 93% of moves on record. Expect rate sheets to follow.

upcoming.why: A hotter than expected print pushes mortgage rates up.

upcoming.why: A hotter than expected print pushes mortgage rates down.

alerts.label: Core CPI surprise beyond 1 sigma
alerts.detail: Core CPI came in at 0.335 versus trailing 24m mean, a 1.0 sigma surprise. Bearish for rates
alerts.why: Core CPI is the highest-variance monthly release for mortgage rates. A hot print reprices the entire curve within minutes.

alerts.label: 10Y Treasury moved 5 bp or more
alerts.why: The 10-year is the primary input to mortgage pricing. A 5 bp move is roughly 5 bp of eventual mortgage rate, arriving with a one to two day lag.
